<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
There's an important architectural issue: `main.spec` is shared across Windows, macOS, and Linux.

A global onefile setting would also affect Linux builds and could break macOS app bundle expectations.

macOS currently also builds as onedir because `main.spec` omits BUNDLE. Three fixes are under consideration: making the spec platform-conditional, forcing onefile via the Windows build script, or creating a Windows-specific spec.

The chosen approach is to make `main.spec` platform-conditional: onefile for Windows, COLLECT for macOS and Linux. `main.py` needs fixing to load frozen DLLs via `_MEIPASS`. `build_exe.py` should drop the misleading `mne collect_all` fallback and align with onefile expectations. CI comments and artifact expectations may also need updating.

The Windows onefile EXE will use `console=True` and `upx=True`. `main.py` must call `add_dll_directory(sys._MEIPASS)` on Windows to locate `hidapi.dll` inside the frozen archive. Linux will remain onedir.

The CI workflow omits `pylsl`, `pystray`, and `pillow`, but the user did not ask to fix CI. The focus remains on producing a complete single-file executable.

The plan is finalized. `main.spec` will be modified directly because `build_exe.py` prefers it. The Windows onefile will bundle `hidapi` and `liblsl` as required. `pystray` and `pillow` may be added for tray support. macOS and Linux
</details></think>
